html:
The Syrian refugee crisis is the flight of millions of people from the Syrian civil war, which began in 2011. About half of Syria's pre-war population of some 22 million was forced from their homes, one of the largest displacements since the Second World War.

The war grew out of the Arab Spring protests, which the government of Bashar al-Assad met with force. Barrel bombs, sieges, chemical attacks and the rise of the Islamic State emptied whole cities such as Aleppo and Homs.

  • About six to seven million people were displaced inside Syria.
  • Turkey took the most refugees, over three million.
  • Lebanon took over a million, at times a quarter of its population, and Jordan several hundred thousand.
  • In 2015 over a million people, many of them Syrians, crossed into Europe, most heading for Germany.

Many lived for years in camps or poor city housing, with children out of school. Assad's government fell in December 2024, and some refugees began to return.
